name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean in a Twin Cities suburban district
Long-serving incumbent Betty McCollum with a large fundraising edge
Challenger Paul Wikstrom raised only $28k with negligible cash
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to McCollum: an D+18 district, incumbency, and a dominant money advantage against a barely funded challenger. Markets and the baseline agree this is safely Democratic, so no evidence justifies moving away.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against McCollum or a polling surprise would be the only realistic path to tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Betty McCollum seeks another term in this St. Paul-area district, which leans Democratic by 18 points. She has raised over $1.2 million and holds nearly $500,000 on hand, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised about $28,000 with almost no cash remaining. No outside groups are active in the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets price McCollum's chances at roughly 95%, and the absence of any general-election polling reflects how little doubt surrounds the contest. The district's partisan lean, incumbency, and financial imbalance all point the same direction, making this one of the safest House seats for Democrats this cycle.
